observations: The comments API accepted visibility working_team from a Legal Team Member, although the composer offers only Legal Only and the team audience. The walkthrough used this only to stand in for older Working Team comments.
Global reminder lead times in this lab are 30, 14, 7, 1, and 0 days, not the initial 7, 1, and 0. The article allows for an organization change.
After Jonas Weber left the C-147 team, his old /portal/requests/123 link showed the Portal request home page (What do you need from Legal?) with no conversation, rather than a not-found message.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

The work lab is shared with other DOC-029 agents; their records and notifications appear in the bells and lists. Assertions used DOC-029 conversations records, comment ids, and mail subjects to separate this walkthrough's events.

Events that trigger notifications, fixture Requests, conversions, team changes, Tasks, two Key dates, invitations, timezones, and one stand-in working_team comment were arranged through the API as the acting role; the article steps under test were followed in the browser.

Mail absence was observed after the pg-boss queue had no pending jobs plus a 4 to 5 second quiet window, paired with positive deliveries through the same worker; this bounds the lab, not an arbitrary relay.

Morning rounds were queued as notification.morning-round jobs in the lab's pg-boss queue rather than waiting for the hourly cron; the worker ran them with its real clock and rules. The UTC fallback for an unsaved timezone was not isolated.

Not exercised: filing as a New Version, Portal History for business Field edits and legal-only Fields, the unread badge's exclusion of removed comments in isolation, a lead time present in both lists, a Key date whose every selected person has left at round time, Knowledge-only briefings, Entity Obligation reminders, and spam or relay faults.
